slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Only copy. FUN_0803a8b0 reads all 64 EEPROM blocks (512B) into a staging buffer, then accepts the copy only if struct u32 at 0x11C equals struct u32 at 0x00 XOR 0x5A5A5A5A AND the byte-sum over struct 0x000..0x123 (checksum field zeroed) equals the u32 stored at 0x120. On success it memcpys 292 bytes to the live RAM struct; on failure it sets an invalid flag and leaves RAM untouched. No backup copy, no generation counter.

checksums.name: struct_byte_sum
checksums.formula_detail: u32 sum of all struct bytes 0x000..0x123 (292 bytes) with the 4 stored-checksum bytes at 0x120..0x123 treated as zero; stored zero-extended as u32_le at 0x120. Magic gate checked first: u32_le at 0x11C must equal u32_le at 0x00 XOR 0x5A5A5A5A (constant is _DAT_0803a93c in FUN_0803a8b0, value recovered from sav-01 bytes). Struct bytes are obtained from the raw .sav by reversing every 8-byte EEPROM block (FUN_08045d40 stores each block's u16s from param_2+6 downwards).

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 helper: writes src/dst/count|0x80000000 to inferred DMA3 registers (0x040000D4 block, literal pool unresolved in decompilation), programs wait-state value, polls DMA busy bit 0x8000. Used for both EEPROM command-send and data-receive directions.
Same DMA3 helper used with (stack, 0x0D000000) to send the serial command/address bitstream to the EEPROM.

EEPROM block read: builds start bits + MSB-first block address on stack, DMA-writes addr_bits+3 halfwords to 0x0D000000, DMA-reads 0x44 halfwords back, unpacks 64 bits into 4 u16 at param_2+6 downwards (causes per-8-byte-block reversal vs raw .sav). Returns 0 on success; caller in callgraph.json is recorded via func_ reference, callgraph lists no FUN callees for 0x0803a8b0.
EEPROM config select. Called with 4 by the save reader, matching 512-byte/64-block geometry; 0x40 and default select other config structs never used by the save path in the corpus.

Save reader/validator: FUN_08045c78(4), 64x FUN_08045d40 into staging buffer, magic check at struct 0x11C, byte-sum check at 0x120, FUN_08046028 memcpy of 0x124 bytes to live RAM struct on success; sets invalid flag on failure.
Computes magic comparison (word0 XOR 0x5A5A5A5A) and byte-sum over 0x124 bytes with checksum field zeroed.

Memsets 0x124 bytes to zero via FUN_08046110 (memset). Target buffer identity (staging vs live struct) unproven because literal pool values are unresolved; no EEPROM write, so this alone does not erase the device. No callers in callgraph.json.

caller_chains.trigger_context: Save load (boot/continue). Upstream caller of 0x0803ab28 is not in the corpus: callgraph.json lists no callers and the function ends in an unrecovered jumptable tail-call.
ram_fields_updated: live RAM save struct (292 bytes, memcpy destination literal unresolved) on validation success
invalid flag byte set to 1 on validation failure

fields.name: seed_key_word
fields.update_mechanism: Set by the (not-in-corpus) serializer before flush; reader derives expected magic as this word XOR 0x5A5A5A5A. Identical in partial and completed images of the same save, so it is not a generation counter.
fields.evidence: FUN_0803a8b0: puVar1[0x47] == (*puVar1 ^ _DAT_0803a93c). On sav-01 after rev8 transform: 0xCE40CC1C ^ 0x941A9646 = 0x5A5A5A5A.

fields.name: name_aaa_candidate
fields.update_mechanism: Written by serializer as part of payload; reader only copies it. No code in corpus interprets it as text.
fields.evidence: Bytes 41 41 41 followed by 0x00 at offset 7 in the verified struct image. Consistent with a default name/initials field, unproven.

fields.name: header_pad_07

fields.update_mechanism: Checksummed and memcpy-copied as a block; never individually accessed in the corpus. Presumed progress/flags storage at default zero in these early saves.

fields.name: magic_word
fields.update_mechanism: Serializer stores struct word0 XOR 0x5A5A5A5A here before flush; reader compares before attempting the checksum.

fields.name: checksum_word
fields.update_mechanism: Serializer zeroes this field, sums all 292 struct bytes, stores the sum here (inferred as writer inverse of the verified reader). Reader saves, zeroes, recomputes, compares.
fields.evidence: FUN_0803a8b0 sum loop over 0x124 bytes; sav-01 stored 0x479 = computed 0x479 (see checksums.verified_on_samples).

open_questions: EEPROM write driver and save serializer are absent from the supplied 102-function corpus: no function bit-bangs a write command to 0x0D000000, stores the magic word at struct 0x11C, or stores the byte-sum at 0x120. Their existence is proven by the sav-00 (partial, invalid) to sav-01 (complete, valid) transition between frames 1325 and 1374, but addresses, write-opcode bits, block write order beyond ascending inference, and retry/verify behavior are unknown.

Exact RAM addresses of the staging buffer (_DAT_0803a938 in FUN_0803a8b0), the live save struct (memcpy destination uRam0803a940), the valid/invalid flags, and the FUN_0803abc8 clear target are unresolved literal-pool values in the supplied Ghidra text, so ram_addr is null in all fields rather than guessed.

Upstream callers of the load wrapper 0x0803ab28 and of the struct-clear 0x0803abc8 are not in callgraph.json (every function ends in an unrecovered jumptable tail-call), so the exact game-state trigger for load/erase, and which gameplay functions mutate payload fields before a flush, cannot be mapped from this corpus.

Semantics and exact types/endianness of payload bytes at struct 0x08..0x0F and the 268 reserved bytes at 0x10..0x11B are unknown: both samples are the same early/default save (payload identical), and no function in the corpus accesses them individually. The fuzzing plan in the report is designed to resolve them.
Whether FUN_08045c78 geometries other than 4 (e.g. 0x40) are used by any non-save EEPROM consumer is out of scope of the traced save path; the save reader always selects 4.

sav-00's zero blocks at struct 0x10..0x27 with erased 0xFF from 0x28 onward suggest the flush writes blocks in ascending order and was interrupted or still in progress at frame 1325, but the writer is not in the corpus to confirm write granularity (per-block vs burst) or timing.
